text:
maria: quick check — when clients omit Content-Type on POST /v2/generate we currently reply text/plain in prod. should runtime coerce to application/json (and parse body as json) or respond 415?
liam: my +1 is: accept missing Content-Type (tolerate common clients) but always respond application/json. SDKs expect object responses.
anika: small note — our SDK decodes null vs absent differently for 'details' field. need a clear rule before changing codec.
kevin: agree with liam. on input: try to parse as JSON if body looks like JSON, otherwise treat as text input. on output: always set Content-Type: application/json. add a header to signal lenient input handling.
tia: what do we do about unknown extra keys returned by model plumbing? drop them, or keep under metadata.extras/warnings? some product clients read unknown keys today.
olga: proposal: we keep unknown keys but surface a metadata.warnings: ["unknown_keys_present"] array. warnings is optional and empty when clean. that makes it non-breaking for most clients.
james: metadata.warnings sounds fine but it technically changes our schema contract. can we make it optional and only set when we detect unexpected shape?
anika: yes optional is fine. SDKs should ignore unknown keys by default. we should add a lint rule that disallows adding new top-level keys without a compatibility note.
api-lint-bot: [lint] rule request recorded: require compat-note for new top-level response keys. ticket TRACK-482 created.
maria: ok action items: 1) runtime: accept missing Content-Type, parse heuristically, but respond application/json (kevin to implement, due EOD Tue). 2) spec: add optional metadata.warnings array and doc guidance that clients must ignore unknown keys (anika + james, due Thu). 3) add api-contract-lint rule (olga to add TRACK-482 tests). 4) sdk: update decoding guidance (liam to coordinate).
kevin: quick example for server behavior:
```
Request: POST /v2/generate (no Content-Type)
Body: {"prompt":"hi"}
Response: 200
Content-Type: application/json
{ "result": "...", "metadata": { "warnings": [] } }
```
kevin: if body is plain text we treat as prompt string and still respond JSON.
james: edge: do we ever return 204? i'd prefer never — always 200 with JSON body even for empty result to avoid client parse errors.
anika: agreed, returning an empty JSON object beats 204 in our SDKs.
maria: thanks team — i'll post the spec blurb after the PRs land. ping if you need to block rollout. :thumbsup:
